what_it_does: Training large AI models across many chips requires splitting the model's layers across devices — a technique called pipeline parallelism. Existing systems split layers in a straight line (stage 1, stage 2, stage 3...), but modern AI models are not actually linear; their computation forms a branching graph (a DAG — directed acyclic graph — where some layers feed into multiple successors or receive input from multiple predecessors). GraphPipe treats the model as the branching graph it really is, partitions the graph into stages that can run simultaneously on different device groups, and schedules mini-batches of training data through those parallel branches. This reduces idle time caused by one branch waiting for another, improving overall throughput.
